subtitle: How a Chauhana king carved his play into stone, and how later hands walled it up

panels.shot: epic low-angle wide of a colonnaded temple-college courtyard, half in sunlight, half in shadow
panels.action: Vigraharaja IV stands in royal robes beside a great stone slab, stylus in hand, as rows of pillars around him fade into the later arches of Adhai-din-ka-Jhonpra in the distance.

dialogue.text: Ajmer, twelfth century: a warrior-king writes a Sanskrit drama on stone for Sarasvati—only for those very stones to be built into a mosque wall within a lifetime.

i18n.hi: १२वीं सदी का अजमेर: एक वीर-राजा सरस्वती के लिए पत्थरों पर संस्कृत नाटक लिखता है—और वही पत्थर जल्दी ही मस्जिद की दीवार बन जाते हैं।

panels.shot: wide aerial of twelfth-century Ajmer nestled among the Aravalli hills at dawn
panels.action: The city of Ajmer lies in a basin ringed by low hills, its fort crowning a rocky height, smoke from hearths rising as the first light brushes temples and walls.

dialogue.text: In the middle of the twelfth century, Ajmer was the heart of the Chahamana realm, a hill-ringed capital watching the plains and deserts of north India.

i18n.hi: १२वीं सदी के बीच, पहाड़ियों से घिरा अजमेर चाहमान सत्ता का दिल था, जो उत्तर भारत के मैदानी और रेगिस्तानी इलाकों पर नज़र रखता था।

panels.shot: medium interior of a royal hall, side light falling on a young king amid ministers and warriors
panels.action: Vigraharaja IV, in his thirties, sits straight on a low throne, one hand resting on a sword, the other holding a palm-leaf manuscript, courtiers split between soldiers and scholars around him.

dialogue.text: Vigraharaja IV, called Visaladeva, ruled c.1150 to 1164 CE, remembered in records as both conqueror and patron of Sanskrit learning.

i18n.hi: विग्रहराज चतुर्थ, जिसे विसालदेव कहा गया, लगभग ११५०–११६४ ई. तक राज करता रहा, जिसे अभिलेखों में विजेता और संस्कृत-विद्या का संरक्षक दोनों माना गया।

panels.shot: low-angle medium of the king in a study, lit by an oil lamp
panels.action: In a quieter chamber, Vigraharaja leans over a palm-leaf, stylus poised, lips moving silently as he composes, the sword set aside against the wall.

dialogue.text: Where many kings only listened to poets, inscriptional and literary evidence credits Vigraharaja with composing his own drama, the Harakeli Nataka.

i18n.hi: जहाँ कई राजा सिर्फ कवियों को सुनते थे, शिलालेख और साहित्य विग्रहराज को स्वयं हरकेली नाटक का रचनाकार मानते हैं।

panels.shot: over-the-shoulder close-up of the manuscript, script lines running neat and dense
panels.action: The palm-leaf shows lines of Nagari script, the heading naming Harakeli Nataka, with a marginal note recalling Bharavi’s Kiratarjuniya as inspiration.

dialogue.text: Later scholars, from Dasharatha Sharma to Cynthia Talbot, note that the play echoed Bharavi’s Kiratarjuniya, fitting the king into a long, exacting Sanskrit tradition.

i18n.hi: दशरथ शर्मा से लेकर सिंथिया टैलबॉट तक विद्वान लिखते हैं कि नाटक भारवि के किरातार्जुनीय की गूँज है, जो राजा को कठिन संस्कृत परंपरा की कड़ी बनाती है।

panels.shot: grand wide of a temple-college under construction, scaffolding and stone carvers at work
panels.action: Stones are hoisted by ropes, sculptors chip pillars, and priests consult plans as Vigraharaja points toward a rising sanctum where a statue of Sarasvati is being readied.

dialogue.text: To house such learning, Vigraharaja founded a temple to Sarasvati at Ajmer, with a Sanskrit college attached, where sacred rites and grammar lessons shared the same courtyard.

i18n.hi: इस विद्या के लिए विग्रहराज ने अजमेर में सरस्वती मंदिर और उससे जुड़ा संस्कृत कॉलेज बसाया, जहाँ पूजा और व्याकरण पाठ एक ही आँगन बाँटते थे।

panels.shot: medium shot of the king addressing assembled scholars in the new courtyard
panels.action: Rows of Brahmana teachers and students sit on the stone floor, manuscripts on their laps, as Vigraharaja stands before a newly carved image of Sarasvati, scroll in hand, face intent.

dialogue.speaker: vigraharaja_iv
dialogue.text: Let these halls carry not only my name, but our words.

i18n.hi: इन प्रांगणों में सिर्फ मेरा नाम नहीं, हमारी वाणी गूँजे।

panels.shot: wide interior of a cloister, large stone slabs arranged like open pages
panels.action: Massive dressed stone slabs lie propped against pillars, scribes and masons clustered as Vigraharaja recites from his play, a mason carefully marking guidelines on the rock face.

dialogue.text: Here he attempted something rare: to carve his drama itself onto stone slabs, turning the very fabric of the college into a permanent manuscript.

i18n.hi: यहीं उसने अनोखा प्रयोग किया: नाटक को ही पत्थर की पट्टियों पर उकेरना, ताकि कॉलेज की दीवारें ही चिरस्थायी पांडुलिपि बन जाएँ।

panels.shot: tight side view of chisel meeting stone, with the king supervising closely
panels.action: A sculptor’s chisel taps steadily, each stroke bringing up crisply incised Nagari letters, while Vigraharaja, close by, compares the carved line to the palm-leaf in his hand.

dialogue.text: Epigraphic fragments today preserve only portions, but the style and colophon identify these slabs as Harakeli Nataka, the king’s own composition.

i18n.hi: आज सिर्फ कुछ शिलाखंड बचे हैं, पर शैली और उपसंहार बताते हैं कि ये हरकेली नाटक के टुकड़े हैं—राजा की अपनी रचना।

panels.shot: medium of scholars reading from the stone slabs in the colonnade
panels.action: Young students trace letters on the vertical slabs with their fingers as a teacher chants a verse, Vigraharaja watching from the shadows between two pillars.

dialogue.text: In these pillared galleries, the drama was not just entertainment. It was a carved model of language, meter and royal self-fashioning for the students of Ajmer.

i18n.hi: इन स्तंभित गलियारों में नाटक केवल मनोरंजन नहीं था; वह भाषा, छंद और राजछवि का उकेरा हुआ पाठ था, अजमेर के विद्यार्थियों के लिए।

panels.shot: dramatic upward shot of the Ashokan pillar with new inscription being carved
panels.action: On a lofty stone pillar with Mauryan polish, craftsmen on scaffolds inscribe fresh Nagari lines, while Vigraharaja stands below, looking up at his Delhi-Shivalik record.

dialogue.text: Beyond Ajmer, his Delhi-Shivalik pillar inscription of 1164 CE, cut onto an older Ashokan pillar, boasted of his conquests—stone again used to frame his place in history.

i18n.hi: अजमेर से परे, ११६४ ई. का उसका दिल्ली–शिवालिक स्तंभ-शिलालेख, एक प्राचीन अशोक स्तंभ पर खुदा, उसकी विजयों का ढोल पीटता है—इतिहास में जगह पाने को फिर वही पत्थर।

panels.shot: montage-like wide of the wider region, with caravan routes and frontier forts
panels.action: Caravans move along dusty roads, distant forts dot the horizon, and the faint outline of a frontier facing the north-west hints at approaching powers.

dialogue.text: Yet the world around Ajmer was shifting. Ghurid forces pressed into north India, even as Rajput courts like Vigraharaja’s balanced war, patronage and politics.

i18n.hi: पर अजमेर के चारों ओर दुनिया बदल रही थी। घुरी सेना उत्तर भारत पर चढ़ आ रही थी, और विग्रहराज जैसे राजपूत दरबार युद्ध, दान और राजनीति का संतुलन साध रहे थे।

panels.shot: somber interior of the Sarasvati temple-college at twilight, empty and echoing
panels.action: The once-busy courtyard stands quiet; oil lamps burn low near the goddess, rows of stone slabs line the cloister, an abandoned manuscript lies half-open on a bench.

dialogue.text: Vigraharaja’s reign ended around 1164. Within a generation, his successors would face the shock of defeat at Tarain and the entry of new rulers into Ajmer.

i18n.hi: विग्रहराज का शासन लगभग ११६४ के आसपास खत्म हुआ। एक पीढ़ी के भीतर ही उसके उत्तराधिकारियों को तराइन की हार और अजमेर में नए सत्ताओं के प्रवेश का झटका झेलना पड़ा।

panels.shot: wide shot of Ajmer fort and city under new banners after 1192
panels.action: The skyline of Ajmer shows different standards flying over its fort, armed contingents moving through its streets, the temple-college visible in the middle distance.

dialogue.text: After Prithviraj’s fall in 1192, sources record that Qutb al-Din Aibak, Ghurid general and later Delhi ruler, took Ajmer into his control.

i18n.hi: ११९२ में पृथ्वीराज के पराजय के बाद, स्रोतों में मिलता है कि घुरी सेनापति और आगे चलकर दिल्ली के शासक क़ुतबुद्दीन ऐबक ने अजमेर अपने हाथ में ले लिया।

panels.shot: ground-level wide of the Sarasvati complex amid construction scaffolding and arches forming
panels.action: Workers dismantle parts of the temple-college, stone beams lie stacked, new arches rise; pillars with Hindu carvings stand under the beginnings of a mosque façade.

dialogue.text: Archaeological and epigraphic study shows that Aibak’s builders converted this very Sarasvati temple and college into a congregational mosque later called Adhai-din-ka-Jhonpra.

i18n.hi: पुरातात्त्विक और शिलालेखीय अध्ययन बताते हैं कि ऐबक के कारीगरों ने इसी सरस्वती मंदिर और कॉलेज को जामा मस्जिद में बदला, जिसे बाद में अधाई-दिन-का-झोंपड़ा कहा गया।

panels.shot: close-up of a familiar inscribed slab being lifted and reoriented by workers
panels.action: Two labourers haul a heavy stone slab; its surface bears crisp Sanskrit lines from Harakeli Nataka as they set it sideways into the growing mosque wall.

dialogue.text: In this process, the inscribed drama slabs were reused as building material, their Sanskrit verses literally turned into blocks within the mosque’s fabric.

i18n.hi: इस रूपांतरण में नाटक-शिलाएँ इमारती पत्थर के रूप में दोबारा लगीं; उनके संस्कृत श्लोक सचमुच मस्जिद की दीवारों के बीच ईंटों की तरह जम गए।

panels.shot: interior wide of the newly formed Adhai-din-ka-Jhonpra prayer hall
panels.action: Rows of arches and a broad prayer hall stand complete; pillars show earlier carvings, and in the side walls, faint Sanskrit lines can be seen on some reused stones.

dialogue.text: Modern historians point to Adhai-din-ka-Jhonpra as one of the clearest cases where a pre-existing temple-college was structurally adapted into a mosque, its earlier inscriptions still visible.

i18n.hi: आज के इतिहासकार अधाई-दिन-का-झोंपड़ा को उन सबसे साफ उदाहरणों में गिनते हैं जहाँ एक पुराने मंदिर–कॉलेज को ढाँचागत रूप से मस्जिद में बदला गया, और पुराने अभिलेख अब भी दीवारों पर दिखते हैं।

panels.shot: close-in oblique view of a Sanskrit inscription fragment in the mosque wall
panels.action: A weathered stone in the wall bears partial Nagari lines, gaps where letters have flaked off, while the smooth interior of the mosque stretches beyond.

dialogue.text: The Harakeli Nataka survives today only in such fragments, documented by the Archaeological Survey of India and studied line by line in epigraphic reports.

i18n.hi: हरकेली नाटक अब बस ऐसे ही टुकड़ों में बचा है, जिसे भारतीय पुरातत्व सर्वेक्षण ने दर्ज किया और शिलालेख-रिपोर्टों में पंक्ति-दर-पंक्ति पढ़ा।

panels.shot: modern-era wide shot of a quiet corner of Adhai-din-ka-Jhonpra with a lone researcher
panels.action: A present-day historian stands near the wall with notebook in hand, carefully copying the old Sanskrit letters as tourists drift in the background.

dialogue.text: Scholars like Dasharatha Sharma and Cynthia Talbot, reading these stones, piece together the picture of a poet-king whose literary ambition had to be excavated from a later monument.

i18n.hi: दशरथ शर्मा और सिंथिया टैलबॉट जैसे शोधकर्ता इन पत्थरों को पढ़कर उस कवि-राजा की तस्वीर जोड़ते हैं, जिसकी साहित्यिक साधना को बाद की इमारत से literally खोदकर निकालना पड़ा।

panels.shot: evocative split-frame: half shows Vigraharaja reciting in his college, half shows the same stone now in the mosque wall
panels.action: On one side, Vigraharaja stands before freshly carved slabs, reciting with raised hand; on the other, the identical slab, now part of a wall, bears the same letters, softened with age.

dialogue.text: The romantic subplots of Harakeli Nataka belong to literature, not biography, but its very existence marks Vigraharaja as a ruler who sought to speak in his own Sanskrit voice.

i18n.hi: हरकेली नाटक की प्रेम-कथाएँ साहित्य की हैं, जीवन की नहीं; पर उसका होना ही दिखाता है कि विग्रहराज वह शासक था जो अपनी बात खुद संस्कृत में कहना चाहता था।

panels.shot: final contemplative wide of the mosque-temple complex at sunset, half-lit, half in shadow
panels.action: The Adhai-din-ka-Jhonpra complex stands against a reddening sky; pillars, arches and inscribed stones merge into one silhouette as a bird crosses the fading light.

dialogue.text: Standing here today, among arches built on temple pillars and walls bearing a king’s drama, we see how words, power and stone outlast rulers in ways none of them could plan.

i18n.hi: आज जब हम यहाँ खड़े हैं, मेहराबों के नीचे जो मंदिर के स्तंभों पर टिके हैं, और दीवारों पर उकेले राजा के नाटक के बीच, तो दिखता है कि शब्द, सत्ता और पत्थर शासकों से कहीं ज़्यादा देर तक टिकते हैं—उनके किसी भी ख़ाके से अलग।

subtitle_i18n.en: How a Chauhana king carved his play into stone, and how later hands walled it up
subtitle_i18n.hi: कैसे एक चौहाना राजा ने नाटक पत्थर पर उकेरा, और बाद के हाथों ने उसे दीवारों में दबा दिया
